name: DPW World Heavyweight Championship
epitaph: Won by an 8-man tournament in 1996 and defended almost continuously into 1997: Steven "The Edge" Spector gave way, untracked, to "Devastator" Mick Morton by New Year's Day 1997, who lost it in turn to "Superstar" Steve Sampson at the uncaptured Broken Hearts PPV (14 February 1997). Sampson was still champion, having just survived a Captain Midnight attack, when this wing's own served record breaks off (8 March 1997); the fed's own founder later stated it closed its doors the following April, merging into PCW.

name: DPW Central Valley Championship
epitaph: Created "to pay homage to the CVWF," the predecessor federation whose name lives on in this belt alone. Drac "The Raven" Dravin was awarded it for outlasting a 92-minute Royal Rumble stand in March 1996; by 1997 it belonged to Mr. Robinson, who carried it through an undefeated run the newsgroup's own year-end poll later ranked #16 in all of e-wrestling.

name: DPW Skyweight Championship
epitaph: A weight-limited belt (under 245 pounds) held by the Hitman as of the fed's Motor City Madness PPV in 1996; by the New Year's Bash it belonged to Dan James, defending against King Cobra in a match this wing's own record does not follow to its finish.

name: DPW Network Championship
epitaph: Won by Hollywood in a 16-man "Rage in the Cage" tournament at Motor City Madness (1996); held by Daemon "The Dragon" Dempsey as of the fed's own next newsletter (31 January 1997); billed on Hollywood again by 8 March 1997, defending against The Boogieman in a match this wing's own record does not follow to a confirmed fall.

name: DPW World Tag Team Championship
epitaph: Held by Hardcore Heaven as of Motor City Madness (1996); by the fed's own late-January 1997 newsletter the belts belonged to The New Negaforce, a team sharing its name — but not its full 1996 roster — with an earlier DPW tag team.
